title: Father in Heaven, to Whom Our Hearts
description: Father in Heaven, to Whom Our Hearts in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Henry Ware Jr. wrote these words. They were printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion, compiled by Samuel Longfellow and Samuel Johnson (Boston, 1848), as hymn 41, “For God's Presence”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Fa-ther in heaven, to whom our hearts Would lift them-selves in prayer, Drive from our souls each earth-ly thought, And show Thy pre-sence there.

lines: Father in heaven, to whom our hearts
Drive from our souls each earthly thought,
Each moment of our lives renews
Each moment is itself a gift
To bear us on to God.
Help us to break the galling chains
This world has round us thrown;
Each passion of our hearts subdue,
O Father! kindle in our souls
Of holy love, of grateful trust,

source: A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848)
licence: Public domain: Henry Ware Jr. died in 1843.
credits: Words by Henry Ware Jr. (1794–1843), public domain, as printed in A Book of Hymns for Public and Private Devotion (1848); set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
